why: The install probe validates the packed tarball shape and binary startup. Each mutation
below breaks a different decision the probe makes and must be caught by the named cell.

mutations.name: verifyBinEntry always reports the file exists, so a missing binary is not caught
mutations.find: return { binName: name, binRel: relPath, binPath: absPath, exists: existsSync(absPath) };
mutations.replace: return { binName: name, binRel: relPath, binPath: absPath, exists: true };
mutations.expectRed: a tarball with the bin entry removed FAILS verifyBinEntry
mutations.cell: a tarball with the bin entry removed FAILS verifyBinEntry

mutations.name: the fake registry serves 200 for unknown packages instead of 404
mutations.expectRed: the fake registry returns 404 for unknown packages
mutations.cell: the fake registry returns 404 for unknown packages

mutations.name: the bin path is not joined with the package directory, so it resolves against the wrong root
mutations.expectRed: the bin entry file exists in the extracted tarball
mutations.cell: the bin entry file exists in the extracted tarball

mutations.name: verifyBinEntry returns no bin name when the entry exists
mutations.find: if (entries.length === 0) return { binName: null, binRel: null, binPath: null, exists: false };
mutations.replace: return { binName: null, binRel: null, binPath: null, exists: false };
mutations.expectRed: verifyBinEntry finds the cotal bin entry
mutations.cell: verifyBinEntry finds the cotal bin entry
